number.why: The served RR 0.70 with 95% CI 0.60–0.82 matches the reported all-cause mortality comparison of spironolactone versus placebo at early trial termination, after mean follow-up of 24 months. This confirms the reported RR, not the conflicting HR label or the unestablished intention-to-treat designation.

quotes.span: A total of 822 patients were randomly assigned to receive 25 mg of spironolactone daily, and 841 to receive placebo. The primary end point was death from all causes.
The trial was discontinued early, after a mean follow-up period of 24 months, because an interim analysis determined that spironolactone was efficacious.
There were 386 deaths in the placebo group (46 percent) and 284 in the spironolactone group (35 percent; relative risk of death, 0.70; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.60 to 0.82; P<0.001).

entry.why: The sources establish reduced ejection fraction and a double-blind randomized comparison of spironolactone versus placebo, but neither states adult eligibility or participant ages. The question's adult restriction therefore remains unestablished. Intention-to-treat status is a separate analysis-population issue, not an entry criterion.

quotes.span: In a doubleblind study, we enrolled 1663 patients who had severe heart failure and a left ventricular ejection fraction of no more than 35 percent and who were being treated with an angiotensin-converting-enzyme inhibitor, a loop diuretic, and in most cases digoxin.
A total of 822 patients were randomly assigned to receive 25 mg of spironolactone daily, and 841 to receive placebo.

missed: The lane ruling failed to retain the adult-age evidence gap already identified by the extractor. The HR/RR mismatch and unstated analysis set were already identified; confirmation of the numerical RR does not resolve either.
